description: Real open-access articles from Europe PMC, committed verbatim so the offline suite sees the shapes publishers actually emit rather than the shapes a test author already knew about.

articles.inCorpusBecause: Its publisher-id is a DOI wearing an underscore (10.1177_20552076251406653), which is the shape that provoked the empty-typed-article-id and pattern-recovery defects; it also carries pmcid-ver, two supplementary-material captions, two media captions, eight table-wraps and three figures.
A third publisher-id shape, the journal slug healthcare-14-00097, so the identifier tests are not all measuring one publisher's habits.
The degenerate end of the range: 30 KB, one table, no figures, no supplementary material and no sub-articles. A corpus of only rich articles cannot tell an empty collection from a dropped one.

Peer-review sub-articles (editor-report, decision-letter, reply) whose prose must stay out of the article body, and the only boxed-text caption in the corpus. Boxed-text is the rarest caption host in the wild, 27 of the 2726 captions surveyed, and is one of the hosts the caption-host defect mis-routed.

Carries no publisher-id element at all, so identifier handling is exercised against absence and not only against three present spellings. Also the heaviest supplementary-material caption load in the corpus at twelve, the second commonest caption host in the wild.
